item.title: BadgeFed — Federated Badging
item.description:
Overview

Building BadgeFed, a federated badging platform that recognizes open source contributions through verifiable, decentralized badges. Using ActivityPub federation, badges are issued to contributors’ social identities (Mastodon, Akkoma, and other fediverse accounts) rather than locked into a single platform.

Why Federated Badging

Traditional contribution recognition is fragmented — every project, event, and platform runs its own recognition scheme. BadgeFed reimagines this through the fediverse: a badge is a first-class ActivityPub object that follows the recipient, lives in their identity, and is verifiable by anyone.

item.title: GNOME Foundation Board President
item.description:
Overview

President of the GNOME Foundation Board, providing governance and strategic direction for one of the largest open source desktop communities in the world. The role combines community leadership, organizational stewardship, and advocacy for free software.

Responsibilities

  • Board leadership — presiding over board meetings and guiding strategic discussions
  • Governance — participating in board decisions on foundation policy, budget, and strategic priorities
  • Community leadership — representing the interests of GNOME contributors, users, and the broader ecosystem
  • Fundraising & sustainability — supporting the foundation’s financial health through fundraising initiatives and donor relations
  • Advocacy — promoting GNOME and free software at conferences, in the press, and across the open source ecosystem
  • Community health — helping shape programs that support contributors, engagement, and inclusivity

Impact

  • Contributing to the governance of a foundation that supports GNOME’s worldwide contributor community
  • Strengthening the connection between the foundation, its projects, and the wider open source ecosystem
  • Helping ensure the long-term sustainability of GNOME through sound organizational leadership

item.title: Linux App Summit 2026
item.description:
Overview

Organized the 10th Linux App Summit — a joint GNOME/KDE conference focused on encouraging app development for the Linux platform. Leading the outreach, fundraising, and social media campaign for the event.

Linux App Summit brings together developers, designers, distributions, and ecosystem maintainers to grow the Linux app ecosystem through technologies like Flatpak that enable direct app delivery to users.

Key Responsibilities & Results

  • 10th year organizing LAS and its predecessor, LAS GNOME — a showcase of GNOME and KDE working together
  • Social media transformation — replaced Buffer with Mixpost, a self-hosted social media platform with analytics, editorial workflow, and a collaborative workspace shared across the organizing team (now adopted by GNOME’s own accounts)
  • Multi-platform strategy — expanded beyond Mastodon to LinkedIn, BlueSky, YouTube, and Instagram with per-platform content strategies and goals
  • Influencer engagement — appeared on Tux Digital podcast with Aleix Pol (90 minutes, ~8k views), plus media partnerships with 9to5Linux, It’s FOSS, TuxDigital, and Linux Magazine
  • Record attendance — 110 in-person attendees (venue capacity 100), 156 registered, 71% conversion rate vs the 50% industry average for free events
  • Doubled online viewership — 2k + 2.7k views on the two conference days (more than 2x the previous year), 4.9k aggregate on individual talk videos, ~9.6k total
  • Organic content experiments — a spontaneous podcast-style YouTube conversation with Matthias Clasen (354 views) informed future video strategy

Impact

  • Proved the value of a data-driven, multi-platform outreach strategy for open source events
  • Built a reusable social media infrastructure (Mixpost) now serving GNOME’s own accounts
  • Established a model for breaking out of the fediverse into mainstream developer platforms

item.title: Matrix-Mast-Bot (BoostBot)
item.description:
Overview

A Matrix bot that boosts Mastodon posts based on the Mastodon credentials it’s given — built to help the GNOME community amplify noteworthy posts directly from their Matrix rooms.

How It Works

  • Request — users trigger a boost with !boost <mastodon-url> in a Matrix room
  • Preview — the bot locates the post and shows a preview in the room
  • Approval — authorized users approve or reject via thumbs up/down emoji reactions
  • Boost — after a 5-minute window, the post is boosted by the target account
  • Log — a summary post records who asked, who approved, and when it was boosted

Features

  • Emoji-based approval workflow (thumbs up/down)
  • 5-minute abort window with a 1-minute reminder
  • Authorized-user-only approvals
  • Cleanup of reminder posts after completion
  • Full audit log of boost decisions

Tech

Matrix bot joining the homeserver (gnome.org), no exposed ports — purely room-based interaction. Designed to run on GNOME infrastructure.

item.title: Gitlab Newcomer Bot
item.description:
Project Overview

This is a greeter bot that we’re testing in GNOME to welcome first time contributors and put them into a nurture path. The idea is that contributors who putting their first issue or even their merge/pull request will be required to acknowledge the GNOME Code of Conduct and then provide some helpful links. For MRs, we will also need to set expectation that while their code contribution is valuable that there maybe reasons that they will be rejcted. This will help reduce churn. There are still challenges of course, but having this service will really help provide a more welcoming experience. The project will be tested on the GNOME engagement team before we start convincing other project maintainers to incorporate the bot in their issue/code contributions.

item.title: Ratatoskr MCP Server
item.description:
Project Overview

MCP Server for GNOME integration, providing access to GNOME desktop information and system details via the Model Context Protocol.

Key Points

  • Explore MCP tooling possibilities with the GNOME destop. Using DBus, the MCP server is able to query and set values. An LLM will be able to for instance know what wifi networks are available and be able to determine which is the safest one.
  • Use the MCP server to start various sessions. For instance, the MCP server can set up the a desktop session to have everything ready to code a project. It could even change the lights.

Impact

  • Show the viability of the GNOME in the AI world.

item.title: Hugin MCP Client
item.description:
Project Overview

The MCP client is used as a way to test ratatoskr mcp server. Both projects serve as a way to enable an AI PC idea to connect an LLM to do useful tasks on a laptop or desktop. Hugin supports both a local LLM and Claude. Optimizing the local LLM usecase will be priority.

Key points

  • Build a Linux based “AI PC” on the GNOME desktop
  • Use the MCP client as a way to test the MCP server to try doing tooling requests.
  • Show the viabilty of doing AI on the Linux platform.

Impact

  • Show usefulness of an AI workflow on Linux

item.title: GNOME Foundation Fundraising
item.description:
Project Overview

Supporting the GNOME Foundation’s fundraising efforts through structural guidance and mentorship — helping shape how the organization approaches sustainable funding.

My Role

  • Structural guidance — advising on fundraising structure and approach
  • Mentorship — mentoring those driving the fundraising work
  • Board perspective — helping coordinate which areas need effective fundraising, from the board’s vantage point

Why the Board Run

A key motivation for running for the board was gaining financial oversight — the fundraising work had no direct access to the foundation’s finances, making it hard to ground fundraising strategy in real numbers. Board service provides that oversight and the ability to connect fundraising to the organization’s actual financial picture.

item.title: Containerized GNOME
item.description:
Project Overview

This project is currently not active as GNOME OS still needs some work that will make this more interesting. But this is a technology preview to see if we can run GNOME in a container under kubernetes and be able to support wide scaling.

Features

  • Run GNOME OS in a container and deploy to thousands of instances.
  • Run applicatons in a GNOME OS containers as a ‘meta app container’.
  • Q&A extensions in a robust manner using openQA.
  • Be able to test all extensions based on a tag in GNOME Shell.

Technology Stack

  • Podman + systemd support
  • GNOME OS
    • systemd-sysupdate
    • systemd-homed
  • Buildstream

item.title: oneAPI DevSummit 2025 hosted by UXL Foundation 2025
item.description:
Conference Overview

The UXL DevSummit is a conference brand I created and managed during my tenure at Intel Corporation. The event’s format centers on community-driven content (80%), featuring developers and practitioners demonstrating their work with the oneAPI specification through live demos and technical talks, showcasing the ecosystem’s viability and real-world applications.

I developed the event playbook and served as Master of Ceremonies for this half-day summit, providing the run of show and executive oversight while a contractor handled day-to-day execution. item.title: Linux Plumbers Conference
item.description:
Conference Overview

Founding organizer of the Linux Plumbers Conference — the first conference of its kind bringing together developers from the Linux kernel with user space projects as part of the “plumbing” of the Linux kernel. Now a flagship Linux Foundation conference.

Key Responsibilities

  • Part of the founding team (2008–2009)
  • Built out the conference IT infrastructure to ensure the best attendee experience
  • Invited keynote speakers
  • Recognized specifically for outstanding work in contributing to the success of the conference

Impact

  • Founded a conference that has become a cornerstone of Linux kernel and ecosystem collaboration
  • Now operated under the Linux Foundation
  • Continues to bring kernel developers together with user space projects worldwide
